apoc_text: Remember the commandments, and bear no malice to your neighbour: remember the covenant of the Highest, and wink at ignorance.
old_note: *Remember the commandments, and bear no malice to your neighbour: remember the covenant of the Highest, and wink at ignorance.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 28:7 names the wisdom-stream's articulation of the heart-Torah-substance the King's chapter-closing v.35 lands-on. The framework reads the verse against Matt 18:35's *so likewise shall my heavenly Father do also unto you, if ye from your hearts forgive not every one his brother their trespasses.* The wisdom-stream had named the substance directly: remember-the-commandments AND bear-no-malice to your-neighbour; remember-the-covenant-of-the-Most-High AND wink-at-ignorance. The two-substances are NOT in tension; the two-substances are one-substance — the Torah-internalized produces the substance-of-no-malice; the substance-of-no-malice is the operation-of-the-Torah-internalized. The framework reads this in continuity with Yirmeyahu (Jeremiah) 31:33's new-covenant law-in-the-inward-parts and Yechezk'el (Ezekiel) 36:26-27's new-heart-and-Spirit-causing-the-walking — the wisdom-stream had named the substance the new-covenant brings-to-completion. The grace-that-can-be-lost architecture per Red Line #10 operates here: the walker who-walks-the-substance walks-through-the-door-home; the walker-who-bears-malice-against-the-brother has-not-walked-the-substance-the-grace-was-given-to-form.
new_note: *Remember the commandments, and bear no malice to your neighbour: remember the covenant of the Highest, and wink at ignorance.* (Ecclesiasticus 28:7). *So likewise shall my heavenly Father do also unto you, if ye from your hearts forgive not every one his brother their trespasses.* (Matthew 18:35). Sirach says two things in one line and means them as one: remember the commandments, and bear no malice to your neighbour; remember the covenant of the Highest, and overlook ignorance. Yahusha (Jesus) ends the parable of the unforgiving servant on the same note, that the heavenly Father will deal the same way with anyone who does not forgive his brother from the heart. Remembering the Torah and forgiving the brother are not two different religions; the law written on the heart (Jeremiah 31:33) is what produces a heart without malice. And the parable is plain that the forgiveness a man received can be taken back if he will not extend it; the door home stays a door, and the man who bears malice against his brother has walked away from it.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 28:7 — *Remember the commandments, and bear no malice to your neighbour.* Torah remembered and malice laid down as one thing; at Matthew 18:35 the Father deals the same way with the one who will not forgive *from your hearts*.

apoc_text: The greater you are, the more humble thyself, and you shall find favour before Yahuah (God).
old_note: *The greater you are, the more humble thyself, and you shall find favour before Yahuah (God).* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 3:18 names THE direct wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the kingdom-inversion-of-greatness substance the King teaches at Matt 18:3-4. The framework reads the verse against *except ye be converted, and become as little children, ye shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven. Whosoever therefore shall humble himself as this little child, the same is greatest in the kingdom of heaven.* The wisdom-stream had named the substance directly: the-greater-you-are, the-more-humble-yourself; the substance the King teaches at the assembly-disposition register the wisdom-stream had taught at the wisdom-instruction register. The framework reads this in continuity with the Tanakh-*anawim* (humble-poor) substance pattern (Tehillim (Psalm) 131:1-2; Yeshayahu (Isaiah) 57:15; Yeshayahu (Isaiah) 66:2; Mishlei (Proverbs) 22:4); the apostolic-restatement at 1 Peter 5:5 (citing Mishlei (Proverbs) 3:34) and Yaaqov (James) 4:10. The kingdom-citizen's greatness is measured by the depth of the humility-substance, not by the height of the position-substance.
new_note: *The greater you are, the more humble thyself, and you shall find favour before Yahuah (God).* (Ecclesiasticus 3:18). *And said, Verily I say unto you, Except ye be converted, and become as little children, ye shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven.* (Matthew 18:3). The greater you are, the more humble yourself, Sirach says, and Yahusha (Jesus) makes it the condition of entry: except you be converted and become as little children, you do not enter the kingdom at all. The disciples had just asked who is greatest, and the answer turned their measure upside down, because in the kingdom greatness is measured by how low a man will go, not how high he is set. Sirach was teaching it at a father's table long before the disciples argued about it on the road. The one who humbles himself as a little child is the greatest in that kingdom, which is exactly the favour Sirach said the humble find.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 3:18 — *The greater you are, the more humble thyself, and you shall find favour before Yahuah (God).* The humbling that is the kingdom's entry at Matthew 18:3.

new_note: *Yahuah (God) has cast down the thrones of proud princes, and set up the meek in their stead.* (Ecclesiasticus 10:14). *Whosoever therefore shall humble himself as this little child, the same is greatest in the kingdom of heaven.* (Matthew 18:4). member_note: Ecclesiasticus 10:14 — *cast down the thrones of proud princes, and set up the meek in their stead.* The meek set up in the proud's stead is the child who is greatest at Matthew 18:4.

new_note: *Pride is hateful before Yahuah (God) and man: and by both does one commit iniquity.* (Ecclesiasticus 10:7). *At the same time came the disciples unto Yahusha (Jesus), saying, Who is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven?* (Matthew 18:1). The question itself was the disposition Sirach warned against, and the King answered it by setting a child in their midst. The kingdom does not rank the way the kingdoms of the earth do.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 10:7 — *Pride is hateful before Yahuah (God) and man.* The pride Sirach names is the disposition behind who is the greatest at Matthew 18:1.

apoc_text: You madest Adam, and gavest him Eve his wife for an helper and stay: of them came mankind: you have said, It is not good that man should be alone; let us make to him an aid like to himself.
old_note: *You madest Adam, and gavest him Eve his wife for an helper and stay: of them came mankind: you have said, It is not good that man should be alone; let us make to him an aid like to himself.* Tobit 8:6 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the creation-ordinance marriage-substance in Tobias's-prayer-at-the-marriage-bed — the same Bereshit (Genesis) 2:18 + 2:23-24 substance the King restates at Matt 19:6's *wherefore they are no more twain, but one flesh. What therefore Elohim (God) hath joined together, let not man put asunder.* The framework reads the verse as the wisdom-stream's direct anchor for the Father-joins-the-one-flesh-substance — Tobias prays the creation-ordinance substance over his marriage to Sarah, naming the same substance the King names at the divorce-controversy-pivot. The wisdom-stream and the gospel cohere at the Father-joins-the-one-flesh-substance architecture; what the Father has joined, no human authority undoes at preference. The substance is in continuity with Malachi 2:14-16's *Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel)... hateth putting away* — the Father's-substance toward-putting-away has-always-been-hate-substance, the Mosaic-concession-permission notwithstanding.
new_note: *You madest Adam, and gavest him Eve his wife for an helper and stay: of them came mankind: you have said, It is not good that man should be alone; let us make to him an aid like to himself.* (Tobit 8:6). *Wherefore they are no more twain, but one flesh. What therefore Elohim (God) hath joined together, let not man put asunder.* (Matthew 19:6). On his wedding night Tobias prays the creation back over his marriage: you made Adam and gave him Eve for a helper, and from them came mankind. When the Pharisees pressed Yahusha (Jesus) about divorce he went to the same place, to the beginning, and said that what Elohim (God) has joined no man may put asunder. The library and the gospel stand on the same ground: marriage is the Father's joining, not a human arrangement to be undone at preference. Malachi says he hates putting away (Malachi 2:16), and Tobias's prayer shows a young man who already knew it.
member_note: Tobit 8:6 — *You madest Adam, and gavest him Eve his wife for an helper and stay.* The creation prayed over a marriage bed; *What therefore Elohim (God) hath joined together, let not man put asunder* (Matthew 19:6).

apoc_text: And blessed is the eunuch, which with his hands has wrought no iniquity, nor imagined wicked things against Yahuah (God): for to him shall be given the special gift of faith, and an inheritance in the temple of Yahuah (God) more acceptable to his mind.

The substance is gift, not mandate; the substance is the kingdom-citizen-receiving-the-substance, not the system imposing it. The framework rules out BOTH the Roman-Catholic-mandatory-clerical-celibacy substance the institutional-tradition has imposed AND the Reformation-marriage-mandate-with-no-honored-celibate-substance over-correction. The substance the King-himself walked (1 Corinthians 7:7-8, 32-35's apostle Sha'ul (Paul) walking the same gift-substance) is the substance offered-to-those-to-whom-it-is-given, with the wisdom-stream's-promise-of-inheritance the Isaiah 56 substance carries.
new_note: *And blessed is the eunuch, which with his hands has wrought no iniquity, nor imagined wicked things against Yahuah (God): for to him shall be given the special gift of faith, and an inheritance in the temple of Yahuah (God) more acceptable to his mind.* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:14). *For there are some eunuchs, which were so born from their mother’s womb: and there are some eunuchs, which were made eunuchs of men: and there be eunuchs, which have made themselves eunuchs for the kingdom of heaven’s sake. The inheritance is for the one to whom it is given.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 3:14 — *to him shall be given the special gift of faith, and an inheritance in the temple of Yahuah (God).* The gift behind Matthew 19:12's *he that is able to receive it, let him receive it.*

The framework reads the verse against Matt 19:13's *then were there brought unto him little children, that he should put his hands on them, and pray.* The parents' act is in continuity with the Tanakh-and-wisdom-stream-substance of bringing-children-to-the-Father-for-instruction-and-blessing — the parental-substance of transmitting-the-covenant-to-the-next-generation (Devarim (Deuteronomy) 6:6-7's *and thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house*; Tehillim (Psalm) 78:5-7's substance-of-teaching-the-children). new_note: *Have you children? instruct them, and bow down their neck from their youth.* (Ecclesiasticus 7:23). *Then were there brought unto him little children, that he should put his hands on them, and pray: and the disciples rebuked them.* (Matthew 19:13). Sirach puts children on the list of a man's responsibilities: if you have them, instruct them and bend their necks from their youth. The parents in Matthew 19:13 are doing that when they bring their little ones to Yahusha (Jesus) for his hands and his prayer; it is the Torah's own charge to teach the children carried out in the plainest way, bringing them to the one who teaches. The disciples rebuked the parents, and the Messiah rebuked the disciples, because the bringing was right. Instruction begins with whom you bring your children to.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 7:23 — *Have you children? instruct them, and bow down their neck from their youth.* The parents bringing their children to Yahusha (Jesus) at Matthew 19:13.

The wisdom-stream-substance of children-hearing-the-father is the substance the kingdom-citizen-disposition walks-in: hearing the Father, doing thereafter. The framework reads in continuity with the cause-and-effect-of-hearing per Red Line #11 — *if you hear, you are sons of Avraham (Abraham); you are sons of Adam; you are the seed of promise.* Hearing reveals what was always true. The kingdom-citizens' child-substance is the substance-that-hears the Father's-substance when the Father's-substance speaks. The framework reads this NOT as original-innocence-by-default per the institutional-Christian-tradition (which the Tanakh-and-the-King do not name) BUT as the disposition-substance the four-fold-child-substance carries.
new_note: *Hear me your father, O children, and do thereafter, that you may be safe.* (Ecclesiasticus 3:1). *But Yahusha (Jesus) said, Suffer little children, and forbid them not, to come unto me: for of such is the kingdom of heaven.* (Matthew 19:14). Sirach's picture of safety is children who hear their father and do what he says. Yahusha (Jesus) says the kingdom of heaven is of such, and he says it while his own disciples are forbidding the little ones to come. The kingdom belongs to children not because children are innocent but because a child hears his father's voice and comes when he is called; that is the disposition the kingdom is made of. Hearing is how the Father's children are shown to be his, and the one who hears and does thereafter is the one Sirach says will be safe.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 3:1 — *Hear me your father, O children, and do thereafter.* The children who come when called, of whom the kingdom is, at Matthew 19:14.

new_note: *And when he had called him, he said, My son, when I am dead, bury me; and despise not your mother, but honour her all the days of your life, and do that which shall please her, and grieve her not.* (Tobit 4:3). *And he laid his hands on them, and departed thence.* (Matthew 19:15). Parents brought their children to Yahusha (Jesus) and he laid his hands on them. The library shows a father passing covenant life to the next generation; the gospel shows the King receiving the children their parents bring to him. The two belong together at the household, where the covenant has always been handed down.
member_note: Tobit 4:3 — *My son, when I am dead, bury me; and despise not your mother.* A father handing covenant life to his son; the King laying hands on the children brought to him (Matthew 19:15).

Moses set life and good before Yashar'el (Israel) in the commandments, Sirach calls that inheritance by its name, and the King does not amend it when the question is put to him directly.

new_note: *He that is merciful will lend to his neighbour; and he that strengtheneth his hand keepeth the commandments.* (Ecclesiasticus 29:1). *And he said unto him, Why callest thou me good? there is none good but one, that is, Elohim (God): but if thou wilt enter into life, keep the commandments.* (Matthew 19:17). The framework rules out the inherited-Christian-substance-misreadings: NOT universal-poverty-mandate for-all-kingdom-citizens; NOT Marxist-redistribution at-the-political-substance-level. The substance is heart-Torah-diagnostic; the substance is laying-up-treasure-according-to-the-commandments, which-includes-the-giving-to-the-poor-the-Torah-has-always-commanded (Devarim (Deuteronomy) 15:7-8, Mishlei (Proverbs) 19:17, Tehillim (Psalm) 41:1, Yeshayahu (Isaiah) 58:6-7).
new_note: *Lay up your treasure according to the commandments of the Most High, and it shall bring you more profit than gold.* (Ecclesiasticus 29:11). *Yahusha (Jesus) said unto him, If thou wilt be perfect, go and sell that thou hast, and give to the poor, and thou shalt have treasure in heaven: and come and follow me.* (Matthew 19:21). Sirach says lay up your treasure according to the commandments of the Most High, and it will outprofit gold. Yahusha (Jesus) says it to the young man who has kept the commandments from his youth: sell, give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven. The King's word was a test for one heart, not a command that every disciple become penniless; it found the place where this man's love of neighbour stopped, which was his own possessions. Giving to the poor was never new; the Torah had always commanded it (Deuteronomy 15:7–8), and Sirach is only saying that treasure laid up that way is the kind that lasts.

Being created does not make a man one of the few, and neither does being called. Hearing and keeping do, and those come from what he already was.

new_note: *The greater you are, the more humble thyself, and you shall find favour before Yahuah (God).* (Ecclesiasticus 3:18). *But it shall not be so among you: but whosoever will be great among you, let him be your minister;* (Matthew 20:26). In the kingdom greatness flows downward into service, the exact reverse of the kingdoms around it, and the Messiah is not introducing that reversal; he is restoring what the fathers had already taught and then living it out with a towel.

Yahusha (Jesus) also walked into the temple and cleansed it, but the defilement he drove out had not come from a foreign king. The Maccabees cleansed the temple of a defilement pressed on it from outside; the King cleansed it of the one that grew up inside, in the very priesthood their victory had restored. And presently the fig tree withered away.* (Matthew 21:19). Yahusha (Jesus) came to a fig tree in full leaf, found no fruit, and it withered. Leaves without fruit is the same picture as branches without roots — a show of life with nothing feeding it. The tree stands for the religious leadership of that day, which had the look of the covenant and none of its fruit; it does not stand for the people of Yashar'el (Israel) as a whole. What flourishes without a root does not stand when the wind comes.

apoc_text: Her children shall not take root, and her branches shall bring forth no fruit.
old_note: *Her children shall not take root, and her branches shall bring forth no fruit.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 23:25 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the no-root-and-no-fruit substance the cursed-fig-tree-substance walks. The framework reads the verse against Matt 21:19's *let no fruit grow on thee henceforward for ever.* The Sirach 23 passage walks the substance of the substance-that-walks-against-the-covenant — the children-substance that-shall-not-take-root and the branches-substance that-shall-bring-forth-no-fruit. The substance the King-walks-against at the fig-tree-substance is the same architectural-substance — the leadership-substance has-walked-against the covenant-substance the Father planted-and-hedged-and-tended-for-fruit per the Yeshayahu (Isaiah) 5:1-7 vineyard-substance the King will-walk-out at the wicked-husbandmen-parable at vv.33-46. The leaves-without-the-fruit-substance has-no-root and-shall-bring-forth-no-fruit; the substance is-substantial — the architectural-substance has-walked-against the substance the Father-had-given-the-leadership-to-tend.
new_note: *Her children shall not take root, and her branches shall bring forth no fruit.* (Ecclesiasticus 23:25). *And when he saw a fig tree in the way, he came to it, and found nothing thereon, but leaves only, and said unto it, Let no fruit grow on thee henceforward for ever. And presently the fig tree withered away.* (Matthew 21:19). Sirach says of the adulterous woman that her children will not take root and her branches will bring forth no fruit — what grows from unfaithfulness has nothing underneath it, and nothing comes of it. Yahusha (Jesus) came to the fig tree, found leaves and no fruit, and spoke the same sentence over it: let no fruit grow on you from now on. The tree stands for the leadership that held the vineyard in trust and gave the Father leaves instead of fruit, as the parable of the husbandmen later in the same chapter says plainly. No root, no fruit, and then no fruit forever — the judgment reads the same in both books.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 23:25 — *Her children shall not take root, and her branches shall bring forth no fruit.* Leaves without fruit; the fig tree told *Let no fruit grow on thee henceforward for ever* (Matthew 21:19).
writer_flag: Sirach 23:25 is spoken of the adulterous woman's children; the tie to the cursed fig tree is the shared sentence of no root and no fruit on unfaithfulness. Kept as the old note had it, said plainly.

apoc_text: But to them that repent, he granted them return, and comforted those that failed in patience.
old_note: *But to them that repent, he granted them return, and comforted those that failed in patience.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 17:24 names the wisdom-stream's direct verbal-anchor for the *to-them-that-repent-he-granted-them-return* substance the first-son-substance walks at the parable. The framework reads the verse against Matt 21:29's *I will not: but afterward he repented, and went.* The wisdom-stream-substance the Sirach 17:24 passage walks is the substance-of-the-Father-granting-return-to-the-substance-of-repentance — the substance the first-son-substance walks at the parable-substance. The substance the King-walks at the parable is the substantial-parabolic-substance for-the-substance the wisdom-stream had-named — the substance-of-saying-no-by-the-substance-walked but-afterward-repenting-and-doing is the substance the Father-grants-return-to. The publicans-and-harlots-substance the King names at v.31 walk the substance the wisdom-stream had-named at Sirach 17:24 — afterward-repenting-and-walking-the-substance the substance the system-substance had-categorically-excluded-them-from.
new_note: *But to them that repent, he granted them return, and comforted those that failed in patience.* (Ecclesiasticus 17:24). *He answered and said, I will not: but afterward he repented, and went.* (Matthew 21:29). Sirach says Yahuah (God) grants return to them that repent and comforts those who failed in patience. The first son in the parable said I will not, then repented and went — and he is the one who did the father's will. The publicans and harlots Yahusha (Jesus) names a few lines later walked the same road: a no at first, and then a return. Return is granted to the one who turns, not to the one who said the right word and stayed where he was.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 17:24 — *to them that repent, he granted them return.* Return granted to them that repent is the son who afterward repented, and went at Matthew 21:29.

apoc_text: Distrust not the fear of Yahuah (God) when you are poor: and come not to him with a double heart.
old_note: *Distrust not the fear of Yahuah (God) when you are poor: and come not to him with a double heart.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 1:28 names the wisdom-stream's direct verbal-anchor for the *double-heart* substance the second-son-substance walks at the parable. The framework reads the verse against Matt 21:30's *I go, sir: and went not.* The wisdom-stream-substance the Sirach 1:28 passage walks names the substance the Father-substance does-not-receive — the substance-of-coming-to-him-with-a-double-heart, the substance-of-saying-yes-by-the-mouth-but-walking-no-by-the-substance. The second-son-substance at the parable walks the substance the wisdom-stream had-named at the substance-of-the-double-heart — the substance-of-the-mouth-saying-one-thing-and-the-substance-walking-another. The framework reads the substance in continuity with Matt 7:21-23's *not every one that saith unto me, Lord, Lord* substance + James 1:8's *double minded man is unstable in all his ways* substance + 1 John 2:3-4's *he that saith, I know him, and keepeth not his commandments, is a liar* substance — the substance of the doing-of-the-Father's-will against the substance of the saying-yes-without-doing.
new_note: *Distrust not the fear of Yahuah (God) when you are poor: and come not to him with a double heart.* (Ecclesiasticus 1:28). *And he came to the second, and said likewise. And he answered and said, I go, sir: and went not.* (Matthew 21:30). The second son in the parable says yes with his mouth and no with his feet. Sirach had already named that man: the one who comes to Yahuah (God) with a double heart, one heart for what he says and another for what he does. Yahusha (Jesus) tells the parable to the chief priests and elders, who had answered the Father's call through John with the words of obedience and none of the walking, and the double heart is what he is exposing. A yes that does not go is not a weaker obedience; it is the thing Sirach warns against, and the Father does not receive it.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 1:28 — *come not to him with a double heart.* The second son's *I go, sir: and went not* (Matthew 21:30).

apoc_text: Be not an hypocrite in the sight of men, and take good heed what you speak.
old_note: *Be not an hypocrite in the sight of men, and take good heed what you speak.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 1:29 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the be-not-a-hypocrite-in-the-sight-of-men substance the second-son-substance walks. The framework reads the verse against Matt 21:30's *I go, sir: and went not* + the chief-priests-and-elders-substance the King-walks-against. The wisdom-stream-substance the Sirach 1:29 passage names the substance-of-the-hypocrite — the Greek *hypokritēs* the King uses against the Pharisees throughout the gospel (Matt 6:2, 6:5, 6:16, 15:7, 22:18, 23:13-29, 24:51). The substance the wisdom-stream had-named at Sirach 1:29 is the substance the King-walks-against at the substance of the chief-priests-and-elders walking-the-second-son's-substance — saying-yes-with-the-mouth at the Pharisaic-righteousness-substance but-walking-no at the substance the Father had-laid at the Yochanan (John)-substance. The substance is-substantial — the wisdom-stream and the gospel cohere at the substance-of-the-hypocrite the Father-does-not-receive.
new_note: *Be not an hypocrite in the sight of men, and take good heed what you speak.* (Ecclesiasticus 1:29). *And he came to the second, and said likewise. And he answered and said, I go, sir: and went not.* (Matthew 21:30). Sirach's warning is against being a hypocrite in the sight of men, and against careless speech, and the second son in the parable fails both at once. He speaks the right words, I go, sir, where men can hear them, and then does not go. Yahusha (Jesus) is telling the parable to the chief priests and elders, who had given the Father the public yes and withheld the obedience, which is hypocrisy as Sirach defines it: a performance for the watching crowd with nothing behind it. Take good heed what you speak, Sirach says, because the Father holds a man to what his mouth promised.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 1:29 — *Be not an hypocrite in the sight of men.* The second son's public yes and absent obedience at Matthew 21:30.

apoc_text: My son, have you sinned? do so no more, but ask pardon for your former sins.
old_note: *My son, have you sinned? do so no more, but ask pardon for your former sins. Flee from sin as from the face of a serpent.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 21:1 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the *ask-pardon-for-your-former-sins* substance the Yochanan (John)-baptism-substance walked-out at the wilderness-pericope. The framework reads the verse against Matt 21:32's *Yochanan (John) came unto you in the way of righteousness, and ye believed him not: but the publicans and the harlots believed him.* The wisdom-stream-substance the Sirach 21:1 passage walks names the substance the publicans-and-harlots-substance walked at the Yochanan-substance — the substance of *do so no more* and *ask pardon for your former sins* the Yochanan-substance was the prophetic-articulation-of at the wilderness-pericope. The substance the chief-priests-and-elders-substance refused-to-walk is the substance the wisdom-stream had-named the architecture-of — the substance of *flee from sin* + *do so no more* + *ask pardon*. The first-son-substance walks the wisdom-stream-substance the wisdom-stream had-named; the second-son-substance walks-the-substance-of-saying-yes-without-the-substance-walked.
new_note: *My son, have you sinned? do so no more, but ask pardon for your former sins.* (Ecclesiasticus 21:1). *For John came unto you in the way of righteousness, and ye believed him not: but the publicans and the harlots believed him: and ye, when ye had seen it, repented not afterward, that ye might believe him.* (Matthew 21:32). Sirach opens the chapter with the whole of repentance in one line: stop doing it, and ask pardon for what is past. That is what John came preaching in the wilderness, and Yahusha (Jesus) names who actually did it — the publicans and the harlots believed him and turned, while the chief priests and elders saw it and repented not. The ones with the least standing walked Sirach's counsel; the ones holding the office refused it. Sonship is shown by the turning, not by the title.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 21:1 — *have you sinned? do so no more, but ask pardon for your former sins.* The repentance John preached — the publicans and harlots did it, the office refused it (Matthew 21:32).
writer_flag: Old note quoted part of 21:2 (Flee from sin as from the face of a serpent) as if it were 21:1; the card's point sits in 21:1 alone, so only 21:1 is quoted.

apoc_text: And they that have loathed my law, while they had yet liberty, and, when as yet place of repentance was open to them, understood not, but despised it;
old_note: *And they that have loathed my law, while they had yet liberty, and, when as yet place of repentance was open to them, understood not, but despised it.* 2 Esdras 9:11 names the wisdom-stream's direct verbal-anchor for the substance-of-the-leadership-substance despising-the-substance-of-repentance the Father had opened to them. The framework reads the verse against Matt 21:32's *and ye, when ye had seen it, did not repent afterward, that ye might believe him.* The wisdom-stream-substance the 2 Esdras 9:11 passage walks is the substance-of-the-substance-of-the-leadership's-substance refusing-to-walk-the-substance-of-repentance when-the-place-of-repentance-was-open. The substance is-substantial — the Yochanan (John)-substance was-the-place-of-repentance-open-to-the-substance-of-the-leadership at the wilderness-pericope; the substance-of-the-leadership-substance despised-the-substance-of-repentance the substance-of-the-Father had-opened-to-them. The wisdom-stream and the gospel cohere at the substance-of-the-leadership's-substance walking the second-son's-substance — saying-yes-by-the-substance-of-Pharisaic-righteousness but-walking-not-the-substance-of-repentance the substance-of-the-Father had-opened.
new_note: *And they that have loathed my law, while they had yet liberty, and, when as yet place of repentance was open to them, understood not, but despised it;* (2 Esdras 9:11). *For John came unto you in the way of righteousness, and ye believed him not: but the publicans and the harlots believed him: and ye, when ye had seen it, repented not afterward, that ye might believe him.* (Matthew 21:32). The Most High describes those who loathed his law while they still had liberty, while a place of repentance stood open to them, and despised it. The chief priests and elders are told the same about themselves: John came in the way of righteousness, which is the law's own way, and they did not believe him, and even after watching publicans and harlots repent they did not repent afterward. The open place of repentance was John at the Jordan; they walked past it. Ezra's lament and the King's rebuke describe the same men in the same posture.
member_note: 2 Esdras 9:11 — *when as yet place of repentance was open to them, understood not, but despised it.* The chief priests who would not repent when John came (Matthew 21:32) walked past that open place.

apoc_text: I sent to you my servants the prophets, whom you have taken and slain, and torn their bodies in pieces, whose blood I will require of your hands, says Yahuah (God).
old_note: *I sent to you my servants the prophets, whom you have taken and slain, and torn their bodies in pieces, whose blood I will require of your hands, says Yahuah (God).* 2 Esdras 1:32 names THE direct wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the servants-the-prophets-taken-and-slain substance the parable-of-the-wicked-husbandmen walks-out at vv.34-36. The framework reads the verse against Matt 21:35's *and the husbandmen took his servants, and beat one, and killed another, and stoned another.* The wisdom-stream-substance the 2 Esdras 1:32 passage walks names the same architectural-substance the parable-substance walks-out — the substance of *my servants the prophets* the Father-substance sends + the substance of the leadership-substance taking-and-slaying-and-tearing-the-bodies-in-pieces. The Tanakh-pattern of prophet-killing the King-walks-out at the parable is named at the wisdom-stream-substance at 2 Esdras 1:32 directly. The Father's-substance-of-requiring-the-blood-of-the-prophets is the substance the apostolic-Matt-23:35 substance will-walk-out at the substance-of *the blood of all the prophets, which was shed from the foundation of the world, may be required of this generation.* The wisdom-stream and the gospel cohere at the substance-of-the-leadership's-substance walking-the-substance-of-the-prophet-killing-pattern.
new_note: *I sent to you my servants the prophets, whom you have taken and slain, and torn their bodies in pieces, whose blood I will require of your hands, says Yahuah (God).* (2 Esdras 1:32). *And the husbandmen took his servants, and beat one, and killed another, and stoned another.* (Matthew 21:35). Yahuah (God) says he sent his servants the prophets and the people took them, slew them, and tore their bodies in pieces, and he will require their blood. In the parable the husbandmen take the owner's servants and beat one, kill another, and stone another. The servants are the prophets, the husbandmen are the men set over the vineyard, and the owner who sent them is going to require the blood. The parable is not a new story; the King is telling the leadership of his day the history already written against their fathers, and daring them to finish it.
member_note: 2 Esdras 1:32 — *I sent to you my servants the prophets, whom you have taken and slain.* The husbandmen who beat, killed, and stoned the servants (Matthew 21:35) are the same story.

apoc_text: Thus says the Almighty Yahuah (God), Your house is desolate, I will cast you out as the wind does stubble.
old_note: *Thus says the Almighty Yahuah (God), Your house is desolate, I will cast you out as the wind does stubble.* 2 Esdras 1:33 names the wisdom-stream's direct verbal-anchor for the house-desolate substance the consequence-of-the-killing-of-the-Son walks-into at the parable. The framework reads the verse against Matt 21:39's *and they caught him, and cast him out of the vineyard, and slew him* + Matt 21:41's *he will miserably destroy those wicked men* + the Olivet-discourse-substance at Matthew 24:1-2 (*there shall not be left here one stone upon another, that shall not be thrown down*). The wisdom-stream-substance the 2 Esdras 1:33 passage walks names the substance the substance-of-the-leadership-substance's-walking-against the Father-substance carries-the-consequence-of — *your house is desolate.* The substance is-substantial — the killing-of-the-son-substance the wicked-husbandmen walk-into at v.39 walks-into the substance the wisdom-stream had-named the architecture-of at *your house is desolate.* The Tanakh-pattern of *I never knew you: depart from me, ye that work iniquity* at Matt 7:23 + the *behold, your house is left unto you desolate* at Matt 23:38 cohere with the wisdom-stream-substance at the substance the leadership-substance's-walking-against the Father carries the consequence of.
new_note: *Thus says the Almighty Yahuah (God), Your house is desolate, I will cast you out as the wind does stubble.* (2 Esdras 1:33). *And they caught him, and cast him out of the vineyard, and slew him.* (Matthew 21:39). The sentence in 2 Esdras follows directly on the slaying of the prophets: your house is desolate, I will cast you out as the wind does stubble. The parable follows the same order. After the servants are beaten and killed the son is sent, and the husbandmen cast him out of the vineyard and slay him, and the King asks his hearers what the owner will do to them. The desolate house is the answer. Killing the prophets brought the sentence near; killing the son brought it down, and within a generation not one stone of that house was left on another.
member_note: 2 Esdras 1:33 — *Your house is desolate, I will cast you out as the wind does stubble.* The sentence falls when the husbandmen cast out the son and slay him (Matthew 21:39).

apoc_text: Gather all the tribes of Jacob together, and inherit you them, as from the beginning.
old_note: *Gather all the tribes of Ya'aqov (Jacob) together, and inherit you them, as from the beginning.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 36:11 names THE direct wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the gather-all-the-tribes-of-Ya'aqov substance the chapter-pivot at v.43 walks-into per Red Line #11's ingathering-of-the-paternal-blood-remnant-of-all-twelve-tribes architecture. **FRAMEWORK-MAJOR.** The framework reads the verse against Matt 21:43's *the kingdom of Elohim (God) shall be taken from you, and given to a nation bringing forth the fruits thereof.* The wisdom-stream-substance the Sirach 36:11 passage walks names the substance-of-the-Father-gathering-all-twelve-tribes-of-Ya'aqov-as-the-substance-of-the-inheritance the substance-of-the-beginning had-laid. The *nation* (Greek *ethnos*, SINGULAR-not-plural) the King names at v.43 IS this gathered-bringing-forth-fruit-remnant of the twelve-tribes-of-Ya'aqov the wisdom-stream-substance had-prayed-the-Father-for. The framework rules out THREE inherited readings: (1) the Christian-replacement-theology that-the-categorical-church-replaces-Yashar'el (Israel) collapses the singular-*ethnos* against the wisdom-stream's-direct-naming of the substance as *all the tribes of Ya'aqov*; (2) the Hebrew-Roots-false-inclusion that-the-Torah-keeping-categorical-anyone replaces-the-current-leadership collapses the paternal-blood-substance the *tribes of Ya'aqov* names by-name-by-tribe; (3) the Reformation-sola-fide-without-fruit that-the-bringing-forth-fruit is-incidental collapses the load-bearing-clause itself. The substance is-substantial — the wisdom-stream had-prayed-the-Father-for the substance the King-walks-out at v.43; the substance the apostolic-witness carries-forward at Matt 19:28's *twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Yashar'el* + Acts 26:6-7's *twelve tribes, instantly serving Elohim (God) day and night, hope to come* + James 1:1's *to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad* + Revelation 7:4-8's twelve-tribes-sealed + Revelation 21:12-14's twelve-gates-of-the-twelve-tribes + Ephesians 2:20's apostolic-foundation + 1 Peter 2:9-10's holy-*ethnos* singular addressed to the *strangers scattered* — IS the substance the wisdom-stream had-named, the substance the framework reads at-the-Red-Line-#11-load-bearing-anchor.
new_note: *Gather all the tribes of Jacob together, and inherit you them, as from the beginning.* (Ecclesiasticus 36:11). *Therefore say I unto you, The kingdom of Elohim (God) shall be taken from you, and given to a nation bringing forth the fruits thereof.* (Matthew 21:43). Sirach prays for all the tribes of Jacob to be gathered and inherited as from the beginning. Yahusha (Jesus) tells the chief priests the kingdom will be taken from them and given to a nation bringing forth its fruits; a nation, one, not the nations. That one nation is the gathered tribes of Jacob bearing fruit, the very people Sirach prayed for. It is not the church put in the place of Yashar'el (Israel), and it is not whoever keeps Torah regardless of seed; it is Jacob's own tribes, gathered home and bearing the fruit their leaders in that day would not bring.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 36:11 — *inherit you them, as from the beginning.* The one nation bringing forth fruit (Matthew 21:43) is the gathered tribes of Jacob, not a replacement.

apoc_text: Arise up and stand, behold the number of those that be sealed in the feast of Yahuah (God);
old_note: *Arise up and stand, behold the number of those that be sealed in the feast of Yahuah (God).* 2 Esdras 2:38 names the direct wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the gathered-to-the-feast substance — the *number of those that be sealed in the feast of Yahuah (God)*. The framework reads the verse against Matt 22:9's *go ye therefore into the highways, and as many as ye shall find, bid to the marriage.* The highways-and-hedges-gathering the king-substance sends-the-servants-into is the wisdom-stream's sealed-in-the-feast-of-Yahuah substance — the gathering of the scattered-seed of the twelve-tribes per Red Line #11's ingathering architecture the prophet Hoshea (Hosea) at Hosea 1:9-10, the prophet Yeshayahu (Isaiah) at Isaiah 11:11-12, the prophet Yechezk'el (Ezekiel) at Ezekiel 37:21, and the prophet Zecharyah (Zechariah) at Zechariah 10:8-10 had named. The substance is NOT the categorically-unrelated-nations-grafted-into-the-tree-by-faith-confession substance the inherited-Christian-replacement-theology had collapsed-the-substance-into; the substance is the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the sealed-citizens-of-the-kingdom gathered-to-the-Father's-feast.
new_note: *Arise up and stand, behold the number of those that be sealed in the feast of Yahuah (God);* (2 Esdras 2:38). *Go ye therefore into the highways, and as many as ye shall find, bid to the marriage.* (Matthew 22:9). Esdras is told to stand and look at the number of those sealed in the feast of Yahuah (God). In the parable the first guests would not come, so the king sends his servants into the highways to bid as many as they find to the marriage. The ones found on the highways are not strangers to the king; they are the scattered children whose number he already knows, sealed before the servants ever went out. The feast of Yahuah (God) in 2 Esdras and the marriage in Matthew are the same table, and the guests are gathered in from wherever they were scattered.
member_note: 2 Esdras 2:38 — *behold the number of those that be sealed in the feast of Yahuah (God).* The servants sent into the highways gather them to the marriage (Matthew 22:9).

apoc_text: I Esdras saw upon the mount Sion a great people, whom I could not number, and they all praised Yahuah (God) with songs.
old_note: *I Esdras saw upon the mount Sion a great people, whom I could not number, and they all praised Yahuah (God) with songs.* 2 Esdras 2:42 names the wisdom-stream's vision of the great-people-upon-the-mount-Tsion (Sion) substance — the gathered-multitude at the Father's-feast. The framework reads the verse against Matt 22:10's *and the wedding was furnished with guests.* The wedding-feast filled-with-guests at the king's-table is the wisdom-stream's great-people-upon-the-mount-Tsion-substance — the gathered-citizens of the kingdom the framework reads through the apostle Yochanan (John) at Revelation 7:9-17's *a great multitude, which no man could number, of all nations, and kindreds, and people, and tongues* (the gathered-from-the-scattering substance per Red Line #11, NOT the gathered-from-categorically-unrelated-peoples substance). The wisdom-stream and the apostolic-vision cohere at the gathered-multitude-on-Sion architecture the King's wedding-feast-parable walks-out.
new_note: *I Esdras saw upon the mount Sion a great people, whom I could not number, and they all praised Yahuah (God) with songs.* (2 Esdras 2:42). *So those servants went out into the highways, and gathered together all as many as they found, both bad and good: and the wedding was furnished with guests.* (Matthew 22:10). Esdras sees on mount Sion a great people he could not number, all praising Yahuah (God) with songs. The parable ends with the wedding furnished with guests, gathered from the highways, both bad and good. John saw the same crowd in Revelation 7, a great multitude no man could number, out of all nations. Esdras saw the gathered on the mountain, the parable shows the gathering on the roads, and the next verse in each shows the King coming among them to see who is wearing what.
member_note: 2 Esdras 2:42 — *a great people, whom I could not number, and they all praised Yahuah (God) with songs.* The wedding furnished with guests (Matthew 22:10) is the same gathered crowd.

apoc_text: And in the midst of them there was a young man of a high stature, taller than all the rest, and upon every one of their heads he set crowns, and was more exalted; which I marvelled at greatly.
old_note: *And in the midst of them there was a young man of a high stature, taller than all the rest, and upon every one of their heads he set crowns, and was more exalted.* 2 Esdras 2:43 names the wisdom-stream's direct vision of the young-man-of-high-stature setting-crowns-upon-the-gathered substance — the Messianic-figure crowning the citizens at the Father's-feast. The framework reads the verse against Matt 22:11's *when the king came in to see the guests, he saw there a man which had not on a wedding garment.* The king-substance walking-among-the-guests at the wedding-feast is the wisdom-stream's young-man-of-high-stature among-the-gathered. 2 Esdras 2:43 articulates the substance the gospel-wedding-feast walks at the historical-pivot — the Messianic-king walks-among the gathered-citizens and the substance-walked-with reveals the substance-walked-without (the man-without-the-garment receives no crown; the citizens-walking-in-the-righteousness-of-saints per Revelation 19:8 receive crowns).
new_note: *And in the midst of them there was a young man of a high stature, taller than all the rest, and upon every one of their heads he set crowns, and was more exalted; which I marvelled at greatly.* (2 Esdras 2:43). *And when the king came in to see the guests, he saw there a man which had not on a wedding garment:* (Matthew 22:11). In the midst of the gathered crowd on mount Sion a young man taller than all the rest sets a crown on every head, and the angel tells Esdras a few verses on that this is the Son of Elohim (God) whom they confessed in the world. In the parable the king comes in to see the guests and finds a man with no wedding garment. Both scenes have the King walking among the gathered, and in both what he does depends on what they are wearing; in 2 Esdras the verses before say the gathered have received glorious garments, and these receive crowns. The man without the garment at the marriage receives nothing and is put out. The garment is the righteousness of the saints, and the King himself inspects it.
member_note: 2 Esdras 2:43 — *upon every one of their heads he set crowns, and was more exalted.* The king came in to see the guests and found one without a wedding garment (Matthew 22:11).

The framework reads the verse against Matt 25:32's *and before him shall be gathered all nations: and he shall separate them one from another.* The gathering of Matt 25:32 comes first — the seed brought out of all nations and sifted, the sheep from the goats; then the gathered remnant of the seed of promise (the King's brethren of Matt 25:40), once sifted, judges the nations in the reign, as Wisdom of Solomon 3:8 had named. The Tanakh-parallel at Daniel 7:22 (*judgment was given to the saints of the most High; and the time came that the saints possessed the kingdom*) and Daniel 7:27 (*the kingdom and dominion ... shall be given to the people of the saints of the most High*) carries the same architecture. The framework reads this in continuity with Red Line #11's destination-of-the-gathered-remnant-as-priests-to-the-nations during the millennial-reign + per Revelation 5:10 (*and hast made us unto our Elohim (God) kings and priests: and we shall reign on the earth*).
new_note: *They shall judge the nations, and have dominion over the people, and their Elohim (God) shall reign for ever.* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:8). *And before him shall be gathered all nations: and he shall separate them one from another, as a shepherd divideth his sheep from the goats:* (Matthew 25:32). Before the righteous judge the nations there is a gathering and a sorting. Yahusha (Jesus) says all nations are gathered before him and he separates them as a shepherd divides sheep from goats — the seed brought out of every nation and sifted, the way Ezekiel saw it pass under the rod. Then the sifted remnant, his brethren of Matthew 25:40, does what Wisdom says: judges the nations and has dominion over the people. Daniel saw the same order — *judgment was given to the saints of the El Elyon (most High); and the time came that the saints possessed the kingdom* (Daniel 7:22). The gathering comes first, the reign after.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 3:8 — *They shall judge the nations, and have dominion over the people.* The reign that follows the gathering and sorting of Matthew 25:32 — sheep from goats first, then the saints possess the kingdom.

apoc_text: How is he numbered among the children of Yahuah (God), and his lot is among the saints!
old_note: *How is he numbered among the children of Yahuah (God), and his lot is among the saints!* Wisdom of Solomon 5:5 names the wisdom-stream articulation of the children-of-Yahuah substance + the lot-among-the-saints substance — the substantial-substance the King-of-Yashar'el (Israel) declares at Matt 25:34's *Come, ye blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world.* The wisdom-stream had named the post-judgment-recognition-of-the-righteous at the prefiguring-register; the King-of-Yashar'el (Israel) speaks the operative-form at the gospel-pivot. The framework reads this in continuity with Red Line #11's names-written-in-the-Lamb's-book-from-the-foundation-of-the-world architecture per Revelation 13:8, 17:8; the lot-among-the-saints Wisdom of Solomon names is the inheritance-prepared-from-the-foundation-of-the-world the King-of-Yashar'el (Israel) walks-out. Election precedes hearing; lineage precedes response; the day-of-vindication reveals what was-true-from-before-the-creation.
new_note: *How is he numbered among the children of Yahuah (God), and his lot is among the saints!* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:5). *Then shall the King say unto them on his right hand, Come, ye blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world:* (Matthew 25:34). At the judgment his afflicters discover that the man they despised is numbered among the children of Yahuah (God) and has his lot among the saints. The King says where that lot came from: a kingdom prepared for the blessed from the foundation of the world. It was not assigned on the day; it was prepared before there was a world, and the day only reveals whose it was. Names were written in the Lamb's book from the foundation of the world (Revelation 13:8), and on that day the sheep hear the Shepherd say come, because they were his before they ever heard him.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 5:5 — *How is he numbered among the children of Yahuah (God), and his lot is among the saints.* The lot among the saints is the kingdom prepared from the foundation of the world (Matthew 25:34), revealed on the day, not assigned on it.

apoc_text: Then shall the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him, and made no account of his labours.
old_note: *Then shall the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him, and made no account of his labours.* Wisdom of Solomon 5:1 names THE direct wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the reversal-architecture of the day-of-vindication-of-the-righteous. The framework reads the verse against Matt 25:41's *Then shall he say also unto them on the left hand, Depart from me, ye cursed, into everlasting fire, prepared for the devil and his angels.* The day Wisdom of Solomon prefigured at the wisdom-stream-register is the day Matt 25 enacts — the righteous stand in great boldness; the ungodly are terrified and confess at vv.42-44 the same way Wisdom of Solomon 5:2-6 had named (*they shall be troubled with terrible fear, and shall be amazed at the strangeness of his salvation* + *therefore have we erred from the way of truth*). The wisdom-stream had named the reversal at the prefiguring-passage centuries before; the King-of-Yashar'el (Israel) walks the operative-substance at the sheep-and-goats-judgment. The framework reads the substance carefully — the everlasting-fire was-substantively-prepared FOR-the-devil-and-his-angels (the Watcher-rebellion the apostle-Yahudah (Jude) walked at Jude 6-7 + the apostle-Kefa (Peter) walked at 2 Peter 2:4 + the apostle-Yochanan (John) walks at Revelation 20:10 + 20:14-15); the goats sent toward it are the unfruitful among the gathered, sifted before the reign — not the nations judged for entry into it.
new_note: *Then shall the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him, and made no account of his labours.* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:1). *Then shall he say also unto them on the left hand, Depart from me, ye cursed, into everlasting fire, prepared for the devil and his angels:* (Matthew 25:41). Wisdom and the King are describing the same day from two sides. On that day the righteous stand in great boldness, and the next verse in Wisdom has their afflicters troubled with terrible fear and amazed at a salvation they never looked for, which is exactly the astonishment of those on the left hand asking when they ever saw him hungry or thirsty (Matthew 25:44). Notice what the King says about the fire: it was prepared for the devil and his angels, the fallen ones Jude and Peter say are kept in chains for judgment (Jude 6; 2 Peter 2:4), and the lake in Revelation 20:10 receives the devil first. The goats are sent toward a place that was not made for them. They are the unfruitful among the gathered, sifted before the reign, not the nations being judged for entry.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 5:1 — *Then shall the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him.* The day the righteous stand in boldness is the day of Matthew 25:41; the fire was prepared for the devil and his angels, and the goats are the unfruitful among the gathered.

apoc_text: Marvel not at the works of sinners; but trust in Yahuah (God), and abide in your labour: for it is an easy thing in the sight of Yahuah (God) on the sudden to make a poor man rich.
old_note: *Marvel not at the works of sinners; but trust in Yahuah (God), and abide in your labour: for it is an easy thing in the sight of Yahuah (God) on the sudden to make a poor man rich.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 11:21 names the wisdom-stream articulation of the trust-and-abide-in-your-labour substance — the substantial-substance the faithful-servants at Matt 25:16-23 walked-out the doubling of the talents-substance. The framework reads the verse against Matt 25:21's *Well done, thou good and faithful servant: thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will make thee ruler over many things: enter thou into the joy of thy lord.* The faithful-servants neither marvelled at the works of the sinners-around-them nor stopped-the-labour; they abided-in-the-labour the Father-substance had-given-them, trusting the Father-substance's-knowing per Romans 12:3-8 + 1 Corinthians 12:4-11. The wisdom-stream and the gospel cohere at the abide-in-your-labour substance — the substantial-faithfulness, NOT the substantial-comparative-quantity, is the criterion of the Father-substance's-substantial-commendation.
new_note: *Marvel not at the works of sinners; but trust in Yahuah (God), and abide in your labour: for it is an easy thing in the sight of Yahuah (God) on the sudden to make a poor man rich.* (Ecclesiasticus 11:21). *His lord said unto him, Well done, thou good and faithful servant: thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will make thee ruler over many things: enter thou into the joy of thy lord.* (Matthew 25:21). Sirach tells the labourer not to marvel at how sinners get on, but to trust Yahuah (God) and stay at the work, because he can make a poor man rich in a moment. The faithful servant of the parable did exactly that — did not look sideways, did not stop, traded what he was given — and heard well done. The commendation is for the faithfulness, not the size of the return; the servant with two talents heard the same words as the one with five.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 11:21 — *trust in Yahuah (God), and abide in your labour.* Abiding in the labour is what earns well done, thou good and faithful servant at Matthew 25:21.

apoc_text: A slothful man is compared to a filthy stone, and every one will hiss him out to his disgrace.
old_note: *A slothful man is compared to a filthy stone, and every one will hiss him out to his disgrace.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 22:1 names THE direct wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the slothful-substance the King-of-Yashar'el (Israel) names at the unprofitable-servant. The framework reads the verse against Matt 25:26's *Thou wicked and slothful servant, thou knewest that I reap where I sowed not.* The Greek *oknēre* — slothful, hesitating, shrinking — is the operative-form of the Tanakh-and-wisdom-stream slothful-substance the prophet-Shlomo (Solomon) had walked at Proverbs 6:6-11, 13:4, 19:15, 24:30-34. Sirach 22:1 names the same architecture at the wisdom-stream-register. The substantial-substance is the substantial-failure-of-the-action — the substantial-talent was-not-substantively-put-to-work, was-not-substantively-traded; the substantial-non-action is the substantial-substance the Father-substance walks-against. The wisdom-stream had named the diagnosis; the King-of-Yashar'el (Israel) walks the operative-form at the parable.
new_note: *A slothful man is compared to a filthy stone, and every one will hiss him out to his disgrace.* (Ecclesiasticus 22:1). *His lord answered and said unto him, Thou wicked and slothful servant, thou knewest that I reap where I sowed not, and gather where I have not strawed:* (Matthew 25:26). Sirach's picture is blunt: a slothful man is a filthy stone, and everyone hisses him out to his disgrace. The lord in the parable is just as blunt with the servant who buried his talent — wicked and slothful, he calls him, because the servant knew what his master expected and did nothing. The fault in both is the same: not wickedness done, but the work left undone. Sloth is treated as disgrace in the wisdom book and as judgment in the parable, and it is the same sin in both.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 22:1 — *A slothful man is compared to a filthy stone.* The *wicked and slothful servant* of Matthew 25:26 — the work left undone is the disgrace.

apoc_text: Set him to work, as is fit for him: if he be not obedient, put on more heavy fetters.

The substantial-non-action is the substantial-substance the Father-substance walks-against; the substantial-substance of the consequences-for-the-substantial-failure walks-into the substantial-outer-darkness-substance.
new_note: *Set him to work, as is fit for him: if he be not obedient, put on more heavy fetters.* (Ecclesiasticus 33:28). *Thou oughtest therefore to have put my money to the exchangers, and then at my coming I should have received mine own with usury.* (Matthew 25:27). Sirach's counsel for a servant is to set him to work fit for him, and if he will not obey, to bind him tighter; idleness, the verse before says, teaches much evil. The master in the parable judges his servant by the same measure. The servant was not condemned for losing the money; he was condemned for doing nothing with it, when even handing it to the exchangers would have been work enough. The one who was given a charge and buried it is the one Sirach's heavier fetters were written for.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 33:28 — *Set him to work, as is fit for him: if he be not obedient, put on more heavy fetters..* The servant of Matthew 25:27 was judged for doing nothing with his charge.

new_note: *Work your work betimes, and in his time he will give you your reward.* (Ecclesiasticus 51:30). *His lord said unto him, Well done, good and faithful servant; thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will make thee ruler over many things: enter thou into the joy of thy lord.* (Matthew 25:23). Sirach's last word is a word about timing: do your work early, and the reward comes in his time, not yours. The faithful servant in the parable did exactly that; he worked while the master was away and was paid when the master came back, rule over many things and entry into his lord's joy. The reward is not handed out along the way. Yahusha (Jesus) says *the Son of Adam shall come in the glory of his Father with his angels; and then he shall reward every man according to his works* (Matthew 16:27), and the reigning with him that follows the first resurrection is that reward (Revelation 20:4–6). The work is now; the wages are at his coming.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 51:30 — *Work your work betimes, and in his time he will give you your reward.* The reward comes in his time; at Matthew 25:23 the faithful servant receives it when the master returns, not before.

apoc_text: And he answered me, saying, The most High has made this world for many, but the world to come for few.
old_note: *The most High has made this world for many, but the world to come for few.* 2 Esdras (4 Ezra) 8:1 names THE direct wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the world-to-come-for-few substance — the substantial-substance the substantial-post-harvest-sifting-substance per Red Line #11 walks. The framework reads the verse against Matt 25:10's *and they that were ready went in with him to the marriage: and the door was shut.* The substantial-shut-door is the substantial-substance the substantial-post-harvest-sifting-substance walks-with — the substantial-many-virgins (the substantial-called-substance) divide into the substantial-wise-and-foolish; the substantial-wise-five-with-oil walk-into the marriage; the substantial-foolish-five-without-oil find the substantial-shut-door. 2 Esdras 8:1 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the same architecture — the substantial-world-to-come is for-the-substantial-few; the substantial-many-are-called-but-the-substantial-few-are-chosen per Matt 22:14. The framework reads this carefully per Red Line #11's post-harvest-sifting architecture — the substantial-wheat-after-the-gathering is-sifted-into-wheat-and-chaff; the substantial-foolish-virgins are wheat-that-did-not-bear-the-fruit-of-readiness, NOT tares (the tares were burned at the harvest of Matt 13's wheat-and-tares).
new_note: *And he answered me, saying, The most High has made this world for many, but the world to come for few.* (2 Esdras 8:1). *And while they went to buy, the bridegroom came; and they that were ready went in with him to the marriage: and the door was shut.* (Matthew 25:10). Ten virgins went out to meet the bridegroom, and all ten were called to the wedding; only those who were ready went in before the door was shut. That is Ezra's answer told as a story: this world is made for many, the world to come for few. The five who found the door shut were not strangers; they were virgins with lamps who had gone out to meet him. The few are those found ready when he comes, which is why readiness matters more than having once set out.
member_note: 2 Esdras 8:1 — *this world for many, but the world to come for few.* The shut door of Matthew 25:10 divides the many who set out from the few found ready.

apoc_text: There be many created, but few shall be saved.
old_note: *There be many created, but few shall be saved.* 2 Esdras (4 Ezra) 8:3 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the many-created-but-few-saved substance — the substantial-substance the substantial-post-harvest-sifting-substance walks-into. The framework reads the verse against Matt 25:12's *Verily I say unto you, I know you not.* The substantial *I know you not* of the King-of-Yashar'el (Israel) at the shut-door is the substantial-direct-echo of Matt 7:23's *I never knew you* — the substantial-substance the substantial-form-of-the-substantial-Lord-Lord-confession-without-the-substantial-substance-of-the-substantial-doing walks-into. The substantial-many-created walks the substantial-many-called of Matt 22:14; the substantial-few-saved walks the substantial-few-chosen of the same verse + the substantial-foolish-five who-found-the-shut-door at Matt 25:10. The wisdom-stream and the gospel cohere at the few-saved-many-lost architecture per Red Line #11.
new_note: *There be many created, but few shall be saved.* (2 Esdras 8:3). *But he answered and said, Verily I say unto you, I know you not.* (Matthew 25:12). Many created, few saved: Ezra receives it as the hard rule of the age. The foolish virgins knock at the shut door and hear I know you not, the same word spoken to those who say Lord, Lord and work iniquity (Matthew 7:23). They were among the called and they were not among the few. Ezra's few saved and the bridegroom's I know you not are the two ends of one sentence.
member_note: 2 Esdras 8:3 — *There be many created, but few shall be saved.* The bridegroom's I know you not at Matthew 25:12 is the other end of the same sentence.

apoc_text: And the work shall follow, and the reward shall be shewed, and the good deeds shall be of force, and wicked deeds shall bear no rule.
old_note: *And the work shall follow, and the reward shall be shewed, and the good deeds shall be of force, and wicked deeds shall bear no rule.* 2 Esdras (4 Ezra) 7:35 names the wisdom-stream articulation of the work-shall-follow + the reward-shall-be-shewed substance — the substantial-substance the substantial-post-harvest-sifting-substance walks-out for-the-substantial-substance the substantial-unprofitable-servant walks-into. The framework reads the verse against Matt 25:30's *And cast ye the unprofitable servant into outer darkness: there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.* The substantial-substance the wisdom-stream had named at the work-shall-follow architecture is the substantial-substance the King-of-Yashar'el (Israel) walks-out at the substantial-unprofitable-servant — the substantial-failure-of-the-work walks the substantial-substance into-the-substantial-outer-darkness. The framework reads this carefully — the unprofitable-servant has-been-given-the-substantial-talent (the substantial-grace), has-been-named-as-a-servant (the substantial-relationship), and has-been-cast-into-outer-darkness (the substantial-loss) per Red Line #11's post-harvest-sifting + the substantial-name-can-be-substantively-blotted-out-of-the-Book-of-Life per Exodus 32:33 + Psalm 69:28 + Revelation 3:5 — the substantial-warning is-given-to-the-substantial-wheat-that-did-not-bear-fruit, NOT to-the-substantial-tares.
new_note: *And the work shall follow, and the reward shall be shewed, and the good deeds shall be of force, and wicked deeds shall bear no rule.* (2 Esdras 7:35). *And cast ye the unprofitable servant into outer darkness: there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.* (Matthew 25:30). Ezra is told that at the judgment the work follows and the reward is shown, that good deeds are of force and wicked ones bear no rule. The servant in the parable was given a talent and called a servant; he belonged to the house. What condemned him was not that he was never the master's, but that his work did not follow, and so he is cast into the outer darkness. The warning here is to those inside the household whose deeds bore no fruit, which is why it is so sharp.
member_note: 2 Esdras 7:35 — *the good deeds shall be of force, and wicked deeds shall bear no rule.* The unprofitable servant of Matthew 25:30 was of the house, and his work did not follow him.

apoc_text: Give of your bread to the hungry, and of your garments to them that are naked; and according to your abundance give alms: and let not your eye be envious, when you give alms.
old_note: *Give of your bread to the hungry, and of your garments to them that are naked; and according to your abundance give alms: and let not your eye be envious, when you give alms.* Tobit 4:16 names THE direct wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the give-bread-to-the-hungry + give-garments-to-the-naked substance — the substantial-substance the King-of-Yashar'el (Israel) walks at the six-fold-mercy-criterion of Matt 25:35-36. The framework reads the verse against *For I was an hungred, and ye gave me meat ... naked, and ye clothed me.* Tobit 4:16 names the wisdom-stream's direct verbal-anchor for two of the six-fold-criterion-substance the King-of-Yashar'el (Israel) walks at the sheep-and-goats-judgment. The wisdom-stream had named the substance the substantial Tanakh-prophets walked at Isaiah 58:6-10 (*deal thy bread to the hungry* + *when thou seest the naked, that thou cover him*) + Job 31:16-22 (*If I have seen any perish for want of clothing*) + Proverbs 19:17 (*he that hath pity upon the poor lendeth unto Yahuah (the LORD)*) + Deuteronomy 10:18-19 (*love ye therefore the stranger*). The substantial-substance is NOT the substantial-categorical-charity-program-substance the inherited-Christian-collapse walks; the measure is mercy toward the King's brethren, the seed of promise, and it is the measure by which the gathered are sifted, the sheep from the goats, before the reign.
new_note: *Give of your bread to the hungry, and of your garments to them that are naked; and according to your abundance give alms: and let not your eye be envious, when you give alms.* (Tobit 4:16). *For I was an hungred, and ye gave me meat: I was thirsty, and ye gave me drink: I was a stranger, and ye took me in:* (Matthew 25:35). Bread to the hungry, garments to the naked, alms according to abundance, no envious eye — Tobit gives his son two of the very things the King names at the judgment: *I was an hungred, and ye gave me meat ... naked, and ye clothed me.* Isaiah had said the same, to deal bread to the hungry and cover the naked. This is not a charity program for the world in general; the King says it is mercy done to his brethren, and it is the measure by which the sheep are told from the goats. The library had been teaching that measure in the exile household all along.
member_note: Tobit 4:16 — *Give of your bread to the hungry, and of your garments to them that are naked.* Two of the King's own measures at the judgment, *I was an hungred, and ye gave me meat* (Matthew 25:35).

apoc_text: And stretch yours hand to the poor, that your blessing may be perfected.
old_note: *And stretch yours hand to the poor, that your blessing may be perfected.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 7:32 names the wisdom-stream articulation of the stretch-your-hand-to-the-poor substance — the substantial-substance the King-of-Yashar'el (Israel) walks at the substantial-criterion-of-mercy. The framework reads the verse against Matt 25:36's *I was sick, and ye visited me: I was in prison, and ye came unto me.* Sirach 7:32-35 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the same architecture — *stretch your hand to the poor* (v.32), *fail not to be with them that weep* (v.34), *be not slow to visit the sick: for that shall make you to be beloved* (v.35) — the same six-fold-substance the King-of-Yashar'el (Israel) walks at the sheep-and-goats-criterion. The substantial-substance is the substantial-substance-of-the-blessing-substance-being-perfected-through-the-substantial-mercy-toward-the-substantial-poor — the substantial-substance the inherited-Christian-collapse of-grace-without-fruit explicitly-rules-out; the substantial-substance the framework reads in-continuity-with the new-heart of Ezekiel 36:26-27 the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) gives-into-the-substantial-individual-substance.
new_note: *And stretch yours hand to the poor, that your blessing may be perfected.* (Ecclesiasticus 7:32). *Naked, and ye clothed me: I was sick, and ye visited me: I was in prison, and ye came unto me.* (Matthew 25:36). Sirach says the hand stretched to the poor is what perfects the blessing — the blessing is not finished until it has gone out the door to someone in need. Yahusha (Jesus) sets the same thing as the measure at his judgment seat: the naked clothed, the sick visited, the prisoner visited, and he counts it as done to himself. Sirach keeps going in the next verses — be with them that weep, be not slow to visit the sick — and the list reads like the King's own. This is the fruit of the new heart Ezekiel promised, a heart that keeps his judgments because it has been made able to; a confession that never stretches out its hand has not yet been perfected into a blessing.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 7:32 — *stretch yours hand to the poor, that your blessing may be perfected.* The hand stretched to the poor is the measure the King uses at Matthew 25:36.

apoc_text: Help the poor for the commandment’s sake, and turn him not away because of his poverty.

new_note: *Help the poor for the commandment’s sake, and turn him not away because of his poverty.* (Ecclesiasticus 29:9). *And the King shall answer and say unto them, Verily I say unto you, Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me.* (Matthew 25:40). Sirach says help the poor because the commandment says so, and do not turn him away because he is poor. At the judgment the King says that whatever was done to the least of his brethren was done to him. The mercy Sirach commands is not a charity program; it is the commandment kept, and the King counts it as done to himself because the least of these are his own kin, his brethren, the household of Yashar'el (Israel) scattered and poor. Help the poor for the commandment's sake and you have served the King without knowing his face.
